items.a: No. **Dopamine drives wanting and craving**, not pleasure itself. Anticipation spikes firing from **3–4×/sec baseline to ~30–40×**; most release is anticipatory, not post-reward liking.

items.q: What did the dopamine-depleted rat experiment show?
items.a: Rats still **enjoy food** but **won't move one body length** to get it. Dopamine is about **motivation for pleasure**, not the ability to experience pleasure.

items.q: What happens after every dopamine peak?
items.a: Each pleasure spike mirrors a **craving/pain wave**. Repeated indulgence **lowers peak pleasure** and **raises craving pain** — addiction becomes chasing relief from deficit.

items.q: How do common stimuli compare in dopamine release magnitude?
items.a: Rough scale: **food ~50%**, **sex ~100%**, **nicotine ~150%**, **cocaine/amphetamine ~1000×** relative to baseline release patterns discussed in the recap.

items.q: How do dopamine and "here-and-now" molecules divide labor?
items.a: **Dopamine** biases toward what you don't have (**exteroception**). **Serotonin/endocannabinoids** (plus oxytocin, prolactin) bias toward contentment with what you have (**interoception**). Healthy drive needs both.

items.q: How can mindfulness shift you out of pursuit mode?
items.a: Jon Kabat-Zinn's **one-almond exercise** converts pursuit feeding into present-moment **serotonin/cannabinoid** engagement — savoring instead of chasing the next hit.

items.q: What are Huberman's two procrastinator types?
items.a: (1) people who need **impending-deadline stress** to activate; (2) people with **insufficient baseline dopamine** (clinical vs supplement/pharmacology paths — talk to a professional).

items.q: How do you keep motivation without burning out after every win?
items.a: **Extend the reward arc** — savor after wins without re-engaging the behavior. **Blunt some intermediate celebrations**; intermittent subjective reward (gambling's schedule used for good) preserves long-term pursuit.

items.q: Can belief change how a stimulant works?
items.a: Yes. Students told **caffeine was Adderall** showed **Adderall-like working-memory effects** on **200 mg caffeine** alone — top-down cognition shapes dopamine/adrenaline release.
